terms.meaning: A triangle with all 3 sides equal.
A triangle with all sides of different lengths.
The angle made outside a triangle when one side is extended.
The line from a vertex to the opposite side, or that side extended, at right angles to it. It is also called the height.

items.name: Triangle inequality
items.formula: Each side is less than the sum of the other two

items.name: Quick check
items.formula: Check only the two shorter sides against the longest
items.example: 3, 4, 8: 3 + 4 = 7 is less than 8, so there is no triangle.

items.name: Range of the third side
items.formula: Between the difference and the sum of the other two
items.example: Sides 5 and 8: the third side is more than 3 and less than 13.

items.name: Angle sum
items.formula: The three angles add up to 180°

items.name: Exterior angle rule
items.formula: It equals the sum of the two opposite inner angles
items.example: Inner angles 50° and 60°: the exterior angle is 110°.

items.name: Two angles and a side between them
items.formula: A triangle forms only if the two angles add up to less than 180°
items.example: 100° and 90° add up to 190°, so the arms never meet.

items.name: Named by angles
items.formula: Acute: all below 90°. Right: one 90°. Obtuse: one above 90°.

mistakes.text: If two sides add up to exactly the third, there is no triangle. 3, 4, 7 lies flat, because 3 + 4 = 7.
A triangle cannot have two right or obtuse angles, because the three angles must add up to 180°.
The exterior angle equals the two opposite angles, not all three. It is not 180°.
